questions.question: What unexpected magnetic feature makes the field-induced plateaus of TbB4 distinct from standard Ising and Heisenberg plateau examples?

options.A: Ordered components perpendicular to the applied field remain in plateau phases
options.B: The plateaus occur only above the saturation field
options.C: All plateaus are caused by isolated singlet dimers
options.D: The magnetization is non-quantized and varies continuously across each plateau

questions.rationale: The authors identify TbB4 as a rare case where perpendicular ordered moments coexist with plateau magnetization.
questions.evidence_quote: characterized by ordered perpendicular components in the plateau phase.

questions.question: Which interactions describe the basal-plane magnetic structure and its frustration above TN2?

options.A: Antiferromagnetic J1 and probably antiferromagnetic J2 on the Shastry-Sutherland lattice, with J2 unsatisfied
options.B: Ferromagnetic J1 and antiferromagnetic J2 on an unfrustrated square lattice
options.C: Antiferromagnetic J1 alone, with all bonds minimized in a collinear state
options.D: Ferromagnetic J2 and J3 on a triangular lattice with no nearest-neighbor coupling

questions.rationale: The paper describes the SS lattice with AF J1 and likely AF J2; in the observed structure the J2 bond is not satisfied.
questions.evidence_quote: In this structure, the J2 bond is not satisﬁed.

questions.question: What did the resonant magnetic x-ray diffraction intensity of the (100) reflection establish between 20 and 24 T?

options.A: Substantial magnetic intensity persists across the one-half magnetization plateau
options.B: The magnetic reflection vanishes exactly at the one-half plateau
options.C: Only the nuclear background remains above 16 T
options.D: The one-half plateau is absent at 18 K

questions.rationale: The measured (100) intensity decreases after 16 T but remains constant in the 20–24 T half-plateau interval.
questions.evidence_quote: keeps a constant value between 20 and 24 T, where the one-half magnetization plateau is observed.

questions.question: Why do the authors infer that the persistent (100) plateau-phase reflection mainly arises from ab-plane moments rather than c-axis moments?

options.A: The polarization channel sensitive to c-axis moments is suppressed by the small 6.6° Bragg angle, while the measured component is large
options.B: The incident beam is vertical and cannot scatter from in-plane moments
options.C: The resonance occurs only for moments parallel to the applied c-axis field
options.D: The (100) reflection is a nuclear peak forbidden for c-axis magnetization

questions.rationale: The π–π′ amplitude for the c-axis component is proportional to sin2θ and very small at θ=6.6°; the strong plateau signal therefore identifies ab-plane components.
questions.evidence_quote:
Since θ for the 100 reﬂection
is only 6.6◦, the scattering amplitude for the c-axis com-
ponent is very small.

questions.question: What two types of moments does the proposed simplified model place in the plateau phases?

options.A: Very hard XY-type moments and Ising-like moments
options.B: Soft XY moments and isotropic Heisenberg moments
options.C: Only collinear Ising moments with no transverse components
options.D: Localized singlet dimers and itinerant conduction-electron moments

questions.rationale: The authors propose coexistence of robust planar moments with field-aligned Ising-like moments to reconcile plateaus and transverse order.
questions.evidence_quote:
magnetic structures in the plateau phases consist of very
hard XY -type magnetic moments and Ising-like mag-
netic moments.

questions.question: In the E→∞ toy-model calculation, what discrete states are allowed for spins 1 and 3?

options.A: Two diagonal ab-plane directions and the two opposite z-axis directions
options.B: Only ±x and ±z directions, with y components forbidden
options.C: Four tetrahedral directions with equal x, y, and z components
options.D: A continuous planar angle plus a single positive-z state

questions.rationale: The stated four vectors are the two diagonal XY orientations and the north/south z orientations.
questions.evidence_quote: For rather wide parameter sets, this model has the same ground state as observed.

questions.question: What parameter set did the authors use to illustrate a half-magnetization plateau in the E→∞ model?
questions.rationale: This explicit parameter choice yields the calculated half plateau and the associated structure.
questions.evidence_quote: We took J1 = 2, J2 = 1, J3 = 2, D = 1.

questions.question: How does the model's calculated (100) intensity for the one-half plateau compare with the measured zero-field intensity?

options.A: About one-quarter in the model, broadly consistent with observed 30–50%
options.B: Exactly equal in the model, versus 5% observed
options.C: About 30–50% in the model, versus one-quarter observed
options.D: Nearly zero in both model and experiment

questions.rationale: The calculation predicts roughly 25% of the ground-state intensity, consistent at the order-of-magnitude level with the observed 30–50%.
questions.evidence_quote: The diﬀracted intensity of this structure is about one-quarter of the ground state

questions.question: Why can finite in-plane anisotropy stabilize a one-third plateau state in the authors' frustration argument?

options.A: Planar moments can relax around Ising-like defects and lower exchange energy on otherwise unsatisfied frustrated bonds
options.B: It removes all XY moments so the state becomes a conventional Ising plateau
options.C: It makes the one-half plateau frustrated while leaving the one-third state unfrustrated
options.D: It eliminates the energy gap D and forces continuous magnetization

questions.rationale: With finite E, XY spins can rotate; defects allow local rearrangement that gains exchange energy in the frustrated lattice.
questions.evidence_quote:
all exchange energies have already been
minimized.

questions.question: What important model limitation do the authors identify as necessary to explain the splitting at Hc1?

options.A: Interactions extending beyond J3 must be included
options.B: The model must remove all intersite exchange interactions
options.C: The model must treat the Tb moments as spin-1/2 quantum operators
options.D: The model must include only dipolar coupling and no anisotropy

questions.rationale: They state the simplified short-range model is insufficient to account for the observed splitting at Hc1 without farther-neighbor interactions.
questions.evidence_quote: interactions further than J3 must be included to account for the splitting at Hc1.
